exampleAnswers.title: Exponential Growth Functions With Horizontal and Vertical Shifts

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=3^{x-3}-2?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • First, we plot the graph of $y=3^x.$
  • To plot $y=3^{x-3},$ we shift the graph of $y=3^{x}$ horizontally by $3$ units to the right. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(3,1),$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
  • To plot $y=3^{x-3}-2,$ we shift the graph of $y=3^{x-3}$ vertically by $2$ units down. The point $(3,1)$ moves to $(3,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-2.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=3^{x+5}-4?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • First, we plot the graph of $y=3^x.$
  • To plot $y=3^{x+5},$ we shift the graph of $y=3^{x}$ horizontally by $5$ units to the left. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(-5,1),$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
  • To plot $y=3^{x+5}-4,$ we shift the graph of $y=3^{x+5}$ vertically by $4$ units down. The point $(-5,1)$ moves to $(-5,-3)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=-4.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of $y=-4^{x-2}?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • We take the curve $y=4^x.$
  • Horizontally shift it by $2$ units to the right to give $y=4^{x-2}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(2,1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
  • Then, reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-4^{x-2}.$ The point $(2,1)$ moves to $(2,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

question.text: Which of the following is the graph of the function $y=-\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{x-3}?$
question.explanation:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • We take the curve $y=\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^x.$
  • Horizontally shift it by $3$ units to the right to give $y=\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{x-3}.$ The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(3,1)$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
  • Then, reflect it on the $x$-axis to give $y=-\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^{x-3}.$ The point $(3,1)$ moves to $(3,-1)$ and the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$
